new.title: Walk into Magdeburg Cathedral, Germany's first Gothic cathedral
new.desc: St. Mauritius and St. Catherine Cathedral was begun in 1209 and is regarded as the oldest Gothic cathedral in Germany. Emperor Otto I and his first wife Editha are buried inside, and the twin spires rise about 100 m above the Elbe.
new.tip: Allow an hour inside and look for the sarcophagus of Editha. Tower and special tours run at set times; check the cathedral website.

new.title: See Hundertwasser's Grüne Zitadelle and climb its tower
new.desc: The Green Citadel is one of the last buildings designed by Friedensreich Hundertwasser and opened in 2005. Its pink facade, golden onion domes and rooftop trees surround a courtyard with shops, cafés, a hotel and a theatre.
new.tip: Guided tours run regularly and the courtyard is free to enter. The viewing tower is about 33 m high.
new.q: Grüne Zitadelle, Breiter Weg 9, Altstadt, Magdeburg

new.title: Explore the Romanesque Kloster Unser Lieben Frauen
new.desc: The monastery, founded in the 11th century, is one of the best-preserved Romanesque complexes in Germany. Today it houses a sculpture museum and a concert hall in the former church.
new.tip: The cloister garden is pleasant on dry days and the church hosts concerts; check the museum for current hours.
new.q: Kloster Unser Lieben Frauen, Regierungsstraße 4-6, Altstadt, Magdeburg

new.title: Find the Magdeburger Reiter on Alter Markt
new.desc: The Magdeburg Rider, from around 1240, is considered the oldest free-standing equestrian statue north of the Alps. A bronze copy stands in front of the Old Town Hall, while the sandstone original is kept in the Kulturhistorisches Museum.
new.tip: Combine it with the Rathaus bronze door and the glockenspiel. Visit in the morning before the square fills.
new.q: Magdeburger Reiter, Alter Markt, Altstadt, Magdeburg

new.title: Climb the tower of the Johanniskirche for the city view
new.desc: St. John's is the oldest parish church of Magdeburg, where Martin Luther preached in 1524. Destroyed in 1945 and rebuilt by 1999, it is now an event hall, and its tower has a viewing platform about 52 m high.
new.tip: The tower is open at limited hours, so check before you go. Late afternoon gives the best light.

new.title: Climb the Jahrtausendturm in the Elbauenpark
new.desc: The 60 m Millennium Tower was built for the 1999 federal garden show and is described as Germany's tallest wooden building. Inside, exhibits trace thousands of years of science and technology history.
new.tip: Entry needs a park ticket; check elbauenpark.de for opening dates and the current exhibition.

new.title: Admire the Albinmüller-Turm in Rotehornpark
new.desc: The 60 m tower was built in 1926/27 to plans by Albin Müller and is a landmark of the Stadtpark Rotehorn. In summer it serves as a viewpoint over the Elbe.
new.tip: The platform opens mainly in summer months; check dates before going.

new.title: Step inside the Gruson-Gewächshäuser in Buckau
new.desc: The Gruson greenhouses date from 1895 and go back to the industrialist Hermann Gruson, who was passionate about botany. The glasshouses in the Lenné-designed park hold tropical and desert plants.
new.tip: Entry is cheap and it is a good rainy-day stop. Check the site for current hours.

new.title: Visit the Lukasklause and the Otto-von-Guericke exhibit
new.desc: The medieval defensive tower on the Elbe received an extension in 1900. Inside, an exhibition shows the life and experiments of Otto von Guericke, famous for the Magdeburg hemispheres.
new.tip: Pair it with a walk along the Elbe at Petriförder.

new.title: Visit the Festung Mark, a 19th-century fortress barracks
new.desc: The Kaserne Mark was built between 1863 and 1865 as a defensive barracks of the Magdeburg fortress. Today the brick complex hosts culture events, exhibitions and concerts.
new.tip: Check the event calendar; the courtyard is most atmospheric during concerts.

new.title: Cross the Sternbrücke into Stadtpark Rotehorn
new.desc: The Sternbrücke is an industrial steel bridge from the 1920s at the entrance of the Stadtpark Rotehorn. It was destroyed in 1945, rebuilt after reunification and reopened in 2005.
new.tip: Free and always open; walk it on the way to the Adolf-Mittag-See.

new.title: See the original Magdeburger Reiter in the Kulturhistorisches Museum
new.desc: The museum shows medieval finds, archaeology and the sandstone original of the Magdeburg Rider. The natural history museum shares the building.
new.tip: Plan about two hours; combine with a stop on Hasselbachplatz.

new.title: See the Schiffshebewerk Rothensee, a 1938 ship lift
new.desc: The Rothensee boat lift opened in 1938, closed to freight in 2006 as too narrow and reopened for visitors in 2013. It is the second-oldest of four remaining boat lifts in Germany.
new.tip: Boat trips sometimes start here; check the operator beforehand.

new.title: See the Gründerzeit facades of Hasselbachplatz
new.desc: Hasselbachplatz is the centre of Magdeburg's nightlife, ringed by Gründerzeit facades. The surrounding streets hold bars, restaurants and cafés.
new.tip: Visit by day for the architecture and in the evening for the bars. Parts of the square are a construction site.

new.title: Eat seasonal regional dishes at Restaurant Hoflieferant
new.desc: The restaurant sits about 100 m from the cathedral between the Dom and the Elbe. The menu leans on regional produce, including forgotten vegetables such as purple carrots and golden beets.
new.tip: Dinner Tuesday to Saturday and Sunday lunch; book ahead and confirm hours.

new.title: Have brunch at the Mückenwirt on the Elbe bank
new.desc: The Mückenwirt is a beer garden and restaurant directly on the Elbe with rustic dishes and a popular weekend breakfast and brunch buffet.
new.tip: Brunch is best at weekends; listings show it closed Mondays and Tuesdays, so confirm first.

new.title: Drink a local beer at the Schweizer Milchkuranstalt
new.desc: This beer garden in the Fürstenwallpark is named after a milk-cure spa that stood there over 120 years ago. It serves local draft and bottled beers and grilled snacks such as corn on the cob and sausages.
new.tip: Open in good weather only, with a winter break; guests may bring their own food.

new.title: Taste Tachhell and Stockdunkel at Brauhaus Brewckau
new.desc: Brewckau is a craft brewhouse in the Buckau district, which gave it its name. It brews three permanent beers, Tachhell, Stockdunkel and Chinook, plus seasonal ones, around 50,000 litres a year.
new.tip: Monday and Tuesday are production days; check opening hours first.

new.title: Order robata-grilled dishes at Hyaku Mizu
new.desc: Hyaku Mizu is an Asian restaurant at the Grüne Zitadelle, known for a Japanese robata grill, sushi and an open bar with sake and wine.
new.tip: Book for dinner and try the grilled dishes and the desserts.
new.q: Hyaku Mizu, Breiter Weg 8, Grüne Zitadelle, Magdeburg

new.title: Sip a single-origin coffee at KRÖM Kaffeerösterei
new.desc: KRÖM roasts its own beans from fair-trade farms in Ethiopia, Vietnam and Guatemala. The café is at Alter Markt 5 in the old town centre.
new.tip: Hours are around 11 to 18 on weekdays; confirm before visiting.
new.q: KRÖM Kaffeerösterei, Alter Markt 5, Altstadt, Magdeburg

new.title: Have vegan cake at Café Neuzeit near Hasselbachplatz
new.desc: Café Neuzeit on Einsteinstraße is a very small café known for coffee, homemade vegan cakes and vegan soups.
new.tip: Cash only; closed Mondays and open shorter hours at weekends.

new.title: Have breakfast at the Café am Domfelsen
new.desc: The café at Zum Domfelsen 1 sits by the cathedral rock above the Elbe. Breakfast is served Wednesday to Sunday from 9 to 11:30.
new.tip: Come on a weekend morning and walk the Elbe promenade afterwards.
new.q: Café am Domfelsen, Zum Domfelsen 1, Altstadt, Magdeburg

new.title: Spend a day in the Elbauenpark
new.desc: The park was created for the 1999 federal garden show on a former military site. It has themed gardens, a year-round summer toboggan run reaching 40 km/h and a zipline from the Jahrtausendturm.
new.tip: Winter entry is free; check elbauenpark.de for the season and ticket prices.

new.title: Visit Zoo Magdeburg and its elephants
new.desc: The zoo keeps around 200 species including elephants, giraffes, penguins and chimpanzees.
new.tip: Open 9 to 18 from March to October with an evening ticket after 16:00; adults around 17.50 euros.

new.title: Walk the Elbe promenade at Petriförder
new.desc: The promenade runs along the river below the cathedral and the Lukasklause, with views across to Rotehorn. The Elbe cycle route passes here.
new.tip: Free and best at sunset; extend the walk to the Fürstenwallpark.

new.title: Stroll through Stadtpark Rotehorn to the Adolf-Mittag-See
new.desc: Stadtpark Rotehorn is a large park on an Elbe island with the Adolf-Mittag-See, the Albinmüller-Turm and the Sternbrücke, laid out in the 1920s.
new.tip: Free; walk the loop around the lake or rent a bike.

new.title: Cross the Elbe on the ferry between Rotehorn and the Mückenwirt
new.desc: A small ferry links Rotehornpark with the Mückenwirt on the Elbe bank, according to the Riverside@Night organisers.
new.tip: Seasonal; check the timetable before going.

new.title: See an opera or ballet at Theater Magdeburg
new.desc: Theater Magdeburg stages opera, ballet and plays, with the Opernhaus as its main stage.
new.tip: Book tickets on the theatre website.

new.title: Browse the Magdeburger Weihnachtsmarkt
new.desc: The Christmas market around the Alter Markt and cathedral square is the city's main winter event.
new.tip: Late November to December; bring some cash.
new.q: Weihnachtsmarkt Magdeburg, Alter Markt, Altstadt, Magdeburg

new.title: Walk the Herrenkrugpark and its old lawns
new.desc: The Herrenkrugpark grew from a 17th-century inn and was redesigned in the 19th century under Peter Joseph Lenné, with sculptures and wide lawns.
new.tip: Free; combine with a ride to the Elbauenpark.

new.title: Stroll the Klosterbergegarten and its Schinkel Gesellschaftshaus
new.desc: The Klosterbergegarten was laid out 1825-1829 on a former Benedictine monastery site, designed under Lenné and called Germany's first Volkspark. It holds Karl Friedrich Schinkel's Gesellschaftshaus.
new.tip: Free and quiet; a good weekday stroll.

new.title: Watch a 1. FC Magdeburg match at the MDCC-Arena
new.desc: The MDCC-Arena is the home stadium of 1. FC Magdeburg, with a loud, local crowd on match days.
new.tip: Tickets sell out early; check the club site.
